High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Anuj Singh - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.
Shri Sumit Raghuwanshi - Advocate for objector.

Heard on I.A No.8318/2023 which is an application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C for suspension
of sentence moved on behalf of appellant.

The appellant has been convicted for offence punishable 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 10 years and fine of Rs.100/- with default stipulations and under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC in view of Section 222 of Cr.P.C. wherein no separate sentence has been awarded.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the matter.
It is further submitted that there was a love affair between the appellant and the prosecutrix were in consensual relationship.
As per agreement Exhibit D/2, they were in a relationship since 1 year.
There was a delay of three months in lodging the FIR.
Learned counsel for the appellant has drawn the attention of this Court in paragraphs No.6, 7, 8, 13, 15, 19, 20, 21 & 22 of cross examination of PW/1.

Learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance on (1978) 1 SCC 579 Babu Singh and Ors. Vs.
State of UP wherein it is held that second application for bail when first is dismissed, held, is maintainable.

State of UP
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Senior counsel for the appellant submits that there is clear distinction between mere a breach of promise and giving a false promise to marry.

Only a false promise to marry made with an intention to deceive a women would vitiate the women consent being obtained under misconception of fact but mere breach of promise cannot be said to be a false promise by placing reliance on the judgment dated 09.02.2023 passed by this Court in CRA No.12295/2022 Sumit Mishra Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Dr. Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar Vs. State of Maharastra & Ors (2019) 18 SCC Shubham Raghuwanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39350041/
1 191.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that there is no likelihood of hearing of appeal in near future.
Appellant has already undergone more than 1 year of the awarded sentence.

Hence,
counsel prayed that application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
Learned Panel Lawyer for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector have opposed the application and prays for its rejection.

O n due consideration of the submissions made on behalf of the appellant, o n perusal of the material available on record and without commenting anything on the merits of the case, it would be appropriate to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant.

Accordingly, aforesaid I.A. filed on behalf of appellant is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount if already not deposited and on furnishing personal bond by appellant in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court, for his regular appearance before the concerned trial Court,
the execution of custodial part of the remaining sentence imposed against the appellant shall remain suspended, till the final disposal of this appeal.

The appellant, after being enlarged on bail, shall mark his presence before the concerned trial Court on 07.08.2023 and on all such subsequent dates, which are fixed in this regard by the concerned trial Court.
Certified copy, as per rules.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR (VERMA)) JUDGE DevS Shubham Raghuwanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39350041/
